problems.title: Most Frequent Value
problems.prompt: Return the value occurring most often. If several values tie, return the one that appears first in nums. nums is non-empty.
hints: What information must be remembered while scanning once?
Keep a frequency table and update the best value only when a count strictly improves.
Initialize best to the first value; for each item increment its count, then replace best when that count is greater than the best count.

problems.title: Sorted Pair Exists
problems.prompt: Given an ascending sorted list, return whether two distinct positions sum to target.
hints: How does sorted order tell you which side can be discarded?
Use pointers at both ends; move left for a small sum and right for a large sum.
While left < right, compare nums[left] + nums[right] with target and move exactly one pointer.

problems.title: Balanced Symbols
problems.prompt: Return whether a string containing only ()[]{} is correctly balanced and nested.
hints: Which earlier character must a closing symbol match?
A stack exposes the most recent unmatched opening symbol.
Push openings; for a closing symbol require a non-empty stack with the matching top; finish with an empty stack.

problems.title: First At Least
problems.prompt: Return the first index whose value is at least target in a sorted list, or len(nums) if no such index exists.
hints: Which half can be removed while preserving the first valid index?
Treat every value >= target as a candidate, save it, and continue left.
Initialize answer to len(nums); on a valid midpoint set answer = mid and high = mid - 1, otherwise low = mid + 1.

problems.title: Fewest Hops
problems.prompt: Given an unweighted adjacency dictionary and two nodes, return the fewest edges between them or -1 when unreachable.
constraints: Every neighbor is also a dictionary key
hints: Which traversal discovers nodes in increasing number of edges?
Use a FIFO queue containing node and distance; mark visited when enqueuing.
Start with (start, 0); pop left, return distance at goal, and enqueue unseen neighbors with distance + 1.

problems.title: Pair Sum Indices
problems.prompt: Return the two indices of distinct values that add to target. Exactly one solution exists; return indices in increasing order.
hints: For the current number, what complementary value would complete the target?
Store previously seen value-to-index mappings so the complement can be checked in constant average time.
Scan left to right; before storing nums[i], look for target - nums[i] in seen and return [seen[complement], i].

problems.title: Group Rearranged Words
problems.prompt: Group lowercase words that are rearrangements of the same letters. Preserve the first-seen group order and word order within each group.
hints: What canonical signature is identical for every rearrangement?
Use a sorted word or a 26-count tuple as a dictionary key.
Build a dictionary from signature to list; Python dictionaries preserve insertion order, so returning values preserves first-seen group order.

problems.title: Longest Consecutive Streak
problems.prompt: Return the length of the longest run of consecutive integer values in an unsorted list. Aim for O(n) average time.
hints: If every value starts a forward scan, what repeated work occurs?
Put values in a set and start counting only where value - 1 is absent.
For each sequence start, increment current while current + 1 exists and track the maximum length.

problems.title: Product of the Other Positions
problems.prompt: Return an array where result[i] is the product of all nums values except nums[i]. Do not use division.
hints: Can each answer be split into a product to its left and a product to its right?
Write prefix products into result, then sweep backward with a running suffix product.
Forward: result[i] = prefix then prefix *= nums[i]. Backward: result[i] *= suffix then suffix *= nums[i].

problems.title: Partial Grid Validity
problems.prompt: Return whether a 9x9 partial Sudoku board is valid. Dots are empty; filled digits must not repeat in any row, column, or 3x3 box.
hints: What three uniqueness groups does every filled cell belong to?
Maintain sets for nine rows, columns, and boxes; a box can be identified by (row // 3, col // 3).
For each digit, reject if it is already in any of its three sets; otherwise add it to all three.

problems.title: Most Frequent Values
problems.prompt: Return the k most frequent distinct integers ordered by decreasing frequency; break ties by the value that appears first in nums.
hints: Record both count and first position so the tie rule is explicit.
Frequency is at most len(nums); buckets indexed by frequency avoid sorting all distinct values.
Build buckets of values in first-seen order, then traverse frequencies from high to low until k values are collected.

problems.title: Encode and Decode Strings
problems.prompt: Implement round_trip_strings(values) by designing an unambiguous single-string encoding and decoding it back to the exact original list. Strings may contain any delimiter you choose.
constraints: Strings may be empty or contain digits and punctuation
hints: A delimiter alone is ambiguous when data can contain it. What metadata makes the next boundary known?
Prefix each string with its character length and a separator, then consume exactly that many characters.
Encode as length + '#' + value. Decode by reading digits to '#', parse length, then slice exactly that many characters and repeat.

problems.title: Inventory Reconciliation
problems.prompt: Given before and after lists of item IDs where duplicates represent quantities, return [item_id, delta] pairs for every changed item. Order by first appearance across before followed by after.
constraints: delta is after count minus before count
hints: Can one mapping represent both removals and additions?
Subtract counts from before and add counts from after while separately preserving first-seen order.
Build an ordered union of IDs; update delta[id] by -1 for before and +1 for after; emit nonzero entries in stored order.
